analysis.title: Energy Natural Resources and Utilities Preview: Earnings Ramping, What's Topical - 27 Oct 2026
key_insights: Goldman's desk is hosting a call with Research and the Special Sits desk at 11 AM ET on 27 Oct via Zoom to discuss the EQT/RRC merger and feedback from the prior day.
BKR reports 3Q EPS after the close on 27 Oct. Desk positioning score is 6/10. The desk thinks the stock was well owned by specialist investors for most of 3Q.

BKR has underperformed HAL and SLB over the last month. The desk reads that as a relief rally in the broader oilfield services complex, since positioning in activity-levered Services names was light or underweight.

The desk sees a relatively low bar for BKR's OFSE segment. 3Q OFSE consensus revenue has stepped up over recent months. Guidance has historically been in line with Street numbers, and 4Q OFSE revenue expectations are broadly unchanged.
IET is expected to be the focus on the BKR print, with more industrial investor inbounds lately. The desk is watching commentary on Qatar and LNG most closely.

QatarEnergy headlines over the last week point to contracts and offtakes with non-Middle East players (LNG, WDS, VG). The open question is whether this signals a slowdown, pause or change in rhetoric on the Middle East LNG buildout, and what that means for IET's LNG business.
QatarEnergy has issued several force majeure extensions, including one on the morning of 27 Oct to Italy's Edison through end of December.
Investors are expected to focus on BKR's turbine outlook and the rate of change in orders, with overcapacity narratives present for about two quarters.

DINO: the inland vs coastal refining trade has been very topical on the desk over the last month. The desk thinks it is one of the more crowded trades in Refining (DINO/MPC vs VLO, DK vs PARR). Desk positioning score for DINO is 7/10 into the print.
Street numbers for DINO have moved higher throughout earnings season. The desk expects Refining earnings to be very strong, with the Street at $1.67 bn of Refining EBITDA for 3Q.

DINO focus items, mostly unchanged since 2Q: (1) a CEO announcement expected near-term and whether strategic priorities change, (2) midstream capex, with the Street at $200 mn for 2027 and $245 mn for 2028, (3) refining commentary on crude slate and mix, especially heavy crude given recent moves in differentials.

EXE: this is the new CEO's first earnings call and the first since the EQT/RRC deal, so the desk expects more attention on the print and call. Desk positioning score is 4/10 and expectations for the print itself are low.
The desk reports more client questions on what makes investors interested in EXE again versus other parts of the gas complex. It has discussed 2027 Henry Hub views in a cautious light.

For EXE, the market is looking for: the marketing strategy and growth path after the Twin Eagle deal, long-term offtakes (more topical for gas E&Ps broadly, with generally constructive market feedback), and Haynesville guidance. 4Q production guidance is flat QoQ, and recent gas price pressure could bring flex in guidance.
